title: How red foxes survive the winter
content: Red foxes stay active all winter, hunting mice under the snow by listening for movement and pouncing from above. Their thick coats and bushy tails keep them warm as they roam the forest edge at dawn and dusk.

title: Vulpes vulpes: the world's most widespread wild canid
content: Vulpes vulpes is found across the northern hemisphere, from Arctic tundra to city suburbs. Its adaptability lets it thrive on a varied diet of rodents, fruit and scraps.

title: Life on the tundra: the arctic fox
content: The arctic fox grows a thick white coat in winter that camouflages it against the snow. It scavenges and hunts across the frozen tundra, where few other mammals can survive.

title: Why do wolves howl?
content: Gray wolves howl to keep their pack together and to warn rival packs away from their territory. A chorus of howls can carry for kilometres across forest and tundra.

title: Painted dogs: Africa's team hunters
content: African wild dogs hunt in tightly coordinated packs and share food with the injured and the young. Every animal has its own mottled coat pattern.

title: Bears get ready for hibernation
content: In autumn, black bears eat huge amounts of food to build up fat. A mother and her cubs then settle into a den to sleep through the winter.

title: The social lives of lions
content: Lions are the only truly social big cats, living in prides built around related females. Males defend the territory while the lionesses do most of the hunting.

title: Why hippos spend the day underwater
content: Hippopotamuses stay in rivers and lakes during the day to protect their sensitive skin from the sun. At dusk they come ashore to graze on grass.

title: How camels cope with the desert
content: Dromedary camels store fat in their humps and can go for days without drinking. Their wide feet stop them from sinking into the sand.

title: Silent hunters of the night: barn owls
content: Barn owls have soft feather edges that muffle the sound of their wings. They hunt small rodents over open fields after dark.

title: Raising a golden retriever puppy
content: Golden retriever puppies need early socialisation, short training sessions and plenty of chew toys. Consistency in the first months shapes a calm adult dog.

title: Are black cats really unlucky?
content: Black cats have been tied to superstition for centuries, yet they are no different from any other house cat. Many shelters report that they wait longest to be adopted.

title: Commuting by bicycle in the city
content: Cycling to work saves money and keeps you fit, and in dense cities it is often faster than driving. A good lock and bright lights make the daily ride safer.

title: Why photographers still shoot film
content: A manual rangefinder like the Leica M6 slows you down and rewards patience. Many photographers say that each frame feels more deliberate when film is expensive.

title: Learning to sail: your first season
content: A small sailboat teaches you to read the wind long before you master any knots. Start on sheltered water and learn to tack before heading offshore.

title: What to check before buying a house
content: Look beyond the paint: inspect the roof, the damp course and the electrics before you make an offer. A survey now can save you a fortune in repairs later.

title: Motorcycle touring across Europe
content: Planning a long motorcycle trip means choosing panniers, a good helmet and routes with winding mountain roads. Allow time for fuel stops and border checks.

title: Five habits of great blog writers
content: Great writers draft quickly and edit slowly. They read widely, keep a notebook, and are not afraid to cut their favourite paragraph.

title: Penguin colonies in Antarctica
content: Emperor penguins huddle together on the ice to survive temperatures far below freezing, taking turns to stand in the warm centre of the group.

title: The secret life of toads
content: Toads spend most of their lives on land and only return to ponds to breed. Their dry, bumpy skin helps them hold on to moisture.
